subject: Onboarding: StratoCommerce benchmarking dry run & evidence exchange
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@stratocommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: StratoCommerce — proposed benchmark dry run & evidence exchange

Hi Sanjay,

Thanks again for the kickoff last week. Attached is our proposed benchmarking dry-run plan for the onboarding acceptance test (spreadsheet: stratocommerce-benchmark-plan-20260810.xlsx). Key asks up front:

- Please confirm the SLOs you expect us to validate in the dry run (recommended: P95 latency and sustained throughput targets).
- Share a recent sample traffic profile (headers/avg tokens/peak concurrency) — you can send as CSV; that lets us shape the load generator to match production.
- Can your security team provide IP allowlist windows for the run (we'll need a 3-hour window for the full test, and a separate 30-min canary)?

Our suggested acceptance targets (tentative):
- P95 generation latency < 220ms (512 token budget)
- Sustained throughput: 180 requests/sec with 95% of requests under the P95 latency
- Tail latency (P99) mitigation plan in place (circuit breaker and model fallback)

I've put Monica and Laura in cc — Monica will coordinate the runbook and evidence collection; Laura will export the telemetry artifacts you asked about.

Attachments: stratocommerce-benchmark-plan-20260810.xlsx (load phases, traffic mixes, metrics to collect)

Proposed dry-run window: Thu Aug 13 14:00–17:00 PT (canary at 14:00; ramp to steady-state by 14:30). If that doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Implementation
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: StratoCommerce — proposed benchmark dry run & evidence exchange

Vivek,

Thanks — plan looks good. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Targets: P95 < 200–230ms is acceptable; we will lock to P95 < 225ms for the acceptance sprint.
- Throughput: target sustained 150–180 rps depending on model size. For dry run please aim for 160 rps steady-state at the token mix in the CSV I attached.
- Security: I flagged this to our infra team. They can provide a temporary allowlist window for Aug 13 (14:00–18:00 PT) and will share the IPs by EOD Tues.

Attached: stratocommerce-traffic-profile.csv (sample traffic over 7 days, payload sizes, request paths). I've also cc'd procurement; they want the capacity reservation agreement before we hit production-level tests — procurement@stratocommerce.com can follow up with finance details.

Sanjay

StratoCommerce
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@stratocommerce.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Priom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StratoCommerce — proposed benchmark dry run & evidence exchange

Hi all,

Putting a concise runbook here so everyone has the same expectations. See attached runbook-kv-warmup-and-steady-state.pdf for the full steps. High-level:

Phase 0 — Prep (T-48h)
- Confirm allowlist and account tokens; provide a list of test keys.
- Confirm model shard/variant to run for dry run (we will run both 8-bit quantized and fp16 variants if you want to validate both).

Phase 1 — Canary (14:00–14:30)
- Low concurrency smoke with 10% of steady load; verify correctness and telemetry ingestion.
- KV prefix warmup: run 250 sequential requests to populate common prefixes (we recommend 10–15s gaps to avoid artificial cache bursts).

Phase 2 — Ramp (14:30–14:50)
- Linear ramp from 10% to 100% of target rps (target: 160 rps).
- Monitor tail (P99) and begin snapshotting KV cache hit rates every minute.

Phase 3 — Steady-state (14:50–16:50)
- Maintain steady RPS for 2h with periodic 1-min spikes to 200% to exercise autoscaling.
- Acceptance criteria (pass): P95 < 225ms for >= 95% of the steady-state window; no more than 1 sustained error-rate > 0.5% in any 5-min bucket.

Phase 4 — Evidence collection + wrap (16:50–17:00)
- Package telemetry: per-route latency histograms, token counts, CPU/GPU utilization, autoscale events, and KV cache metrics.

Owners / Ask list:
- Sanjay: confirm the traffic profile is representative for the LLM routes we test.
- Strato procurement: share capacity commit form (DocuSign link in related_links).
- Karthik: please provide the IP allowlist and IB routes; we'll need hostnames for the canary environment.
- Laura: deliver the telemetry artifacts and a dashboard link post-run.

I'll be the primary point-of-contact during the run; if anything deviates we'll execute the fallback (model variant downgrade + reduce concurrency by 50%).

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@stratocommerce.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: StratoCommerce — proposed benchmark dry run & evidence exchange

Heads up on a few infra notes before the run:

- IP allowlist: we'll receive Strato's IPs Tues EOD; our ops team will mirror those into the canary ACL and prod-eviction window. Please confirm which CIDRs to expect.
- Capacity reservations: Vivek — I need a signed capacity commit (DocuSign) for the Dedicated pool so we can spin up the quota for the 2h steady-state. The template is in related_links.
- Monitoring hooks: we'll publish a temporary Prometheus scrape endpoint and a Grafana share (laura will push dashboard access). Please confirm which metric names Strato's SRE expects for latency and token counts.
- Test harness: our load generator will replay the stratocommerce-traffic-profile.csv and maintain header fidelity. Note on KV warmup: use a randomized prefix set of ~5k keys to better mimic production cache entropy; sequential warmup generates unrealistic cache hit rates.

If we see P99 spikes > 700ms during ramp, plan is to immediately reduce concurrency by 40% and revert to the last stable model variant.

I'll be on the call Thu and will coordinate with ops.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: StratoCommerce — proposed benchmark dry run & evidence exchange (confirmation + actions)

Sanjay / Priya / procurement team —

We're set for the dry-run on Thu Aug 13 14:00–17:00 PT (canary at 14:00). Summary of action items and owners: 

1) StratoCommerce: provide final IP CIDRs and confirm the traffic profile is the one attached (Sanjay).
2) Procurement: sign the capacity commitment via DocuSign (link in related_links) so Karthik can reserve quota (procurement@stratocommerce.com).
3) Redwood (Monica): run the 2-hour steady-state and collect telemetry; deliver artifacts as a tarball with README.
4) Redwood (Karthik): configure monitor hooks and ACLs; standby for rollback if P99 > 700ms.
5) Redwood (Laura): provide post-run dashboard link and an artifacts export by EOD Fri.

Accept/reject criteria reminder: pass requires P95 < 225ms for >= 95% of steady-state and error-rate < 0.5% per 5-min bucket. If we fail, we'll do a root-cause triage with Strato within 48 hours and schedule a follow-up run.

For traceability I've added the HubSpot record HS-Record-4238821 to the run artifacts and linked the DocuSign template. Please confirm once procurement signs so we can mark the ticket as green.

Thanks everyone — see you on Thu (I will host the run room).

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Implementation
Redwood Inference
